To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) IRPs were expressed in vitro under defined conditions; (2) The expression of IRP was strain dependent; (3) The expression of the IRPs was medium dependent, and (4) The expression of meningococcal OMVs was strain, medium and temperature dependent.
the expression of IRPs is not dependent on the addition of EDDA to a culture after growth in the presence of a chelatable iron source.

the expression of the IRPs is strain dependent, that the IRP profile is different in different lots of Tryptic Soy broth (TSB), that the expression of IRPs is dependent on the culture medium, and that the IRP expression is dependent on the EDDA concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of IRPs during growth of N. meningitides in defined medium, and the production of IRPs expressing OMVs.
the expression of IRP in vitro during normal growth of N. meningitides in defined conditions.
aspects related to the full expression of meningococcal iron regulated proteins in vitro, in normal growth conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of IRPs during in vitro normal growth of N. meningitides depends on strain and medium, and is not influenced by the concentration of EDDA.
IRP expression in vitro is dependent of the bacterial strain and the culture media.

the expression of meningococcal outer membrane proteins is not affected by the presence of different iron chelators in the culture medium and the expression of meningitis-associated proteins in OMVs is not dependent on the culture conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of IRPs in N. meningitides is strain dependent and that the expression of these proteins can be obtained during normal growth of bacteria in defined conditions.
the IRPs are expressed under defined culture conditions and that OMVs expressing IRPs can be produced by growing the bacteria in iron deficient media.
the IRP expression is not dependent on EDDA concentrations or addition of glucose or use of different media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to use the same culture medium for all strains and to use a defined culture medium, when comparing the expression of IRPs between different meningococcal strains.
the expression of IRPs during growth of Neisseriae is a highly regulated process.
IRP are expressed in vitro under defined conditions and that the expression of these proteins does not require the use of iron chelators.
